text:
maya: Hey team, customer reports streaming responses getting truncated on their side — final JSON chunk never arrives, and clients blow up with "invalid JSON". They say `finish_reason` is missing from the last choice. Request ID: req_0a7b2c. Account: acct-cc123. Any immediate ideas?

sam: Do we have a repro? Browser/EventSource or server-side client? Also which Redwood endpoint are they hitting?

maya: Hitting our hosted stream endpoint: https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams/chat. Repro steps attached from customer:

```
# node repro (EventSource)
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-open-16k', {headers: {Authorization: 'Bearer ...'}});
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('MSG', e.data);
```

When they run it they get a bunch of `data: {...}` events and then the connection closes mid-JSON. Example payload captured by them: 

```
data: {"id":"resp_abc","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}, {"delta":{"content":" final token"}}]}
data: {"id":"resp_abc","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"truncated here`"}}  <-- connection closes abruptly
```

No trailing `data: [DONE]` or `finish_reason` in the last message. They tried reconnecting and getting the remainder does not help.

eric: That smells like an intermediary cutting the TCP stream (idle timeout or buffering) or our runtime not flushing the last chunk. Do we see any proxy/nginx/ELB logs for req_0a7b2c?

maya: I pulled the proxy logs — observed at the edge (nginx):
```
172.31.12.5 - - [12/Mar/2026:17:12:34 +0000] "GET /v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-open-16k HTTP/1.1" 200 - "-" "EventSourceClient/1.0" upstream_response_time: 1.23 request_time: 35.01
```
Looks like request_time ~35s but upstream_response_time only ~1.2s. Also we have this from app logs: `worker-7 wrote 2 chunks, final flush error: write: broken pipe` around the same time.

ingrid: Broken pipe + mismatch between upstream and total request time = connection was kept open but something dropped from client side or LB closed at ~30s. What are our idle timeouts on the edge?

sam: For hosted, Layer7 LB idle timeout is 30s by default for some regions. If the final flush happens after that, LB might tear down the TCP connection. Did the runtime send any keepalive/heartbeat events?

maya: No, this model response didn't emit heartbeats — it's a short generation that finishes with a flush very close to end. Customer's client doesn't automatically retry partial JSON.

support-bot: KB: Streaming best practices: add periodic comment/heartbeat events if generation > 10s; set EventSource reconnect; ensure calls use `Connection: keep-alive`. See https://redwood-inference.com/docs/streaming#keepalive-for-sse

eric: Also check for proxy buffering. If nginx has `proxy_buffering on`, it may wait for bigger buffers before forwarding chunks. For SSE we must disable buffering: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection ''; chunked_transfer_encoding on;`. We already have X-Accel-Buffering off in most locations but not everywhere.

ingrid: Another possibility: TLS termination at CDN/edge — some CDNs force a minimum buffer for response bodies. If that's the cause, heartbeat events (small ping events) will prevent the CDN from closing or aggregating.

sam: Quick mitigation steps we can recommend to customer:
- Add client reconnect logic and tolerate partial events (idempotent resume via Last-Event-ID), or re-request with conversation state.
- Use a short heartbeat every ~8-10s from server if generation can pause.
- Confirm they're not running a proxy that buffers (nginx, corporate proxies).

maya: Customer is using browser EventSource (no corporate proxy), so likely our edge. I'm patching runtime to aggressively flush final chunk and emit a trailing newline + final `data: {"type":"done","finish_reason":"stop"}` line.

sam: Please also capture the raw bytes the runtime sends (tcpdump/strace) for the failing req id, so we can see whether the final bytes ever left our host. If final bytes left but client didn't get them, it's edge/CDN. If final bytes never left, it's our runtime write error.

maya: Attached small repro script I made to simulate flaky flush (useful for QA):
```
# python repro-sim.py
import requests, time
r = requests.get('http://localstack/stream-sim', stream=True)
for chunk in r.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
    if chunk:
        print('CHUNK>', chunk)
    time.sleep(0.1)
# sometimes we intentionally close socket mid-chunk to simulate broken pipe
```

ingrid: Long-term fixes: ensure `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on all edges, enable server-side heartbeats for any streaming responses > 5s, bump LB idle timeout to 90s for streaming routes, and instrument `write()` errors to create an internal alert when write returns EPIPE.

eric: Agreed. I'll file an eng-runtime ticket to: 1) surface write-errors to Sentry, 2) ensure final flush happens with `fsync`-style semantics for our streaming worker, 3) add small heartbeat emit option in runtime config.

support-bot: Created ticket ENG-7832 and linked req_0a7b2c.

maya: I'll reply to customer with these mitigations and ask for their client logs plus whether they can try a region with different edge (us-west vs eu-central) to see if it reproduces. I'll also include our temporary workaround (server heartbeat + keep-alive).

sam: Thanks — tag eng-runtime on the ticket and assign to @eric for triage. Once we confirm it's edge LB idle, we'll push the config change to staging and validate with the repro script. :thumbsup:

maya: Closing loop here once I hear back from customer. If anyone wants to pair on reproducing, ping me.
